title: AI Cost & Observability (CineSpine)
description: Spend and latency for the Gemini calls, from the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, plus the inference cache hit ratio from the app's own cinespine_* instruments. Everything here is pushed by the OTel meter provider. Cost is estimated, not billed -- see the panel description.

list.name: price_in
list.label: Flash input price (USD / 1M tokens)
list.description: Applied to every model whose name does not contain "pro". Gemini Flash and Flash-Lite tiers; check the model legend on the tokens panel.

list.name: price_out
list.label: Flash output price (USD / 1M tokens)
list.description: Output is priced far above input, which is why the split below matters.

list.name: price_in_pro
list.label: Pro input price (USD / 1M tokens)
list.description: Applied to every model whose name contains "pro" (gemini-*-pro, gemini-3-pro-image).

list.name: price_out_pro
list.label: Pro output price (USD / 1M tokens)
list.description: Pro-tier output. Set from the current Google price list; nothing here knows a price.

panels.title: Estimated Spend (selected range)
panels.description: An estimate: token counts multiplied by the price variables above, one pair for Flash-tier models and one for anything with "pro" in its name. Nothing in the codebase knows a price, and no metric here carries dollars -- Grafana's own AI Observability cost panels read gen_ai_usage_cost_USD_sum, which is emitted by the OpenLIT SDK this project removed. So this number moves when Google reprices and nobody edits the variables. Read it as an order of magnitude.

panels.title: Estimated Spend Rate by Model (USD/hour)
panels.description:
Each side is aggregated to gen_ai_request_model before the addition. Without that the two selectors differ on gen_ai_token_type, the binary match finds no partner on either side, and the panel returns an empty vector -- silently, and indistinguishably from no traffic.

Flash and Pro tiers are priced separately, split on the model name; `or` unions the two halves because no model is in both.

15m windows because the OTel reader exports on a 60s interval; a shorter range than roughly 4 export intervals produces gaps rather than a rate.

targets.expr:
(sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_sum{gen_ai_token_type="input", gen_ai_request_model!~".*pro.*"}[15m])) * 3600 / 1e6 * $price_in
 + sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_sum{gen_ai_token_type="output", gen_ai_request_model!~".*pro.*"}[15m])) * 3600 / 1e6 * $price_out)
or
(sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_sum{gen_ai_token_type="input", gen_ai_request_model=~".*pro.*"}[15m])) * 3600 / 1e6 * $price_in_pro
 + sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_sum{gen_ai_token_type="output", gen_ai_request_model=~".*pro.*"}[15m])) * 3600 / 1e6 * $price_out_pro)

panels.title: Tokens per Second by Model and Type
panels.description:
gen_ai_client_token_usage covers every google-genai call the app makes -- character inference, the camera-report vision reader, the multimodal extractor and the Wrap Rescue memo -- because the instrumentation wraps the SDK rather than each call site.

The cinespine_llm_tokens_consumed_total counter this panel replaced was hand-placed at two call sites and recorded total_token_count only, so it both undercounted the run and could not separate input from output.

panels.title: Model Call Latency (mean)
panels.description:
Wall time inside generate_content, per model. This is the one metric name shared with Grafana's packaged AI Observability dashboards, so those panels would populate here; their cost and token panels would not.

Mean from the cumulative sum and count, not histogram_quantile over rate(). p95 is the better question, and the wrong query at this volume: a demo makes a handful of calls, so the bucket counters are flat across any sensible rate window, rate() returns 0 for every bucket, and histogram_quantile of all-zero buckets is NaN -- a blank panel, indistinguishable from no traffic. Verified against a real run. Switch to p95 when calls are continuous enough for the buckets to move.

panels.title: Agent Run Duration (mean)
panels.description:
The agent dimension rather than the model one, recorded by ADK itself in google/adk/telemetry/_metrics.py.

ONE AGENT OF THREE. Only wrap_rescue_handoff_agent -- the inline agent that drafts the memo -- appears here. WrapRescueAgent and AssistantEditorQueueAgent construct an ADK Runner and never call it, so ADK never invokes them and records nothing. Verified against 30 days of Grafana Cloud, not inferred. This panel therefore cannot answer 'which agent is expensive' for the two agents that do the work; it describes memo drafting. See references/findings/agent-telemetry-coverage.md.

ADK adds error_type to failed invocations, which splits the series -- aggregating by gen_ai_agent_name alone folds failures back in on purpose, since a run that died still took time.

Mean rather than p95 for the same reason as the model latency panel: one agent run per demo leaves the bucket counters flat, and a rate-based quantile over flat buckets is NaN.

panels.title: Tool Calls per Agent Run
panels.description:
Mean tool calls per invocation. Read beside the duration panel: a slow agent with a flat tool count is waiting on the model, a slow agent with a rising one is looping.

EXPECT 0, AND EXPECT IT TO STAY 0. Not because this agent happens to have no tools -- because the two agents that do have tools never execute through ADK, and the memo agent that does is given none. WrapRescueAgent and AssistantEditorQueueAgent both declare tools in super().__init__(tools=[...]) that ADK never dispatches; their step loops call those methods directly. The count is correct. It becomes informative only once tool use moves inside an agent that is actually invoked. See references/findings/agent-telemetry-coverage.md.

panels.title: AI Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description:
Reads cinespine_ai_cache_hits_total, the app's own instrument, because the GenAI conventions have no equivalent -- a cache hit never reaches the SDK, so instrumentation that wraps the SDK cannot see it. Until 2026-09-04 this was a prometheus_client counter that nothing scraped on Cloud Run, so this was the one blank panel in production. It is an OTel counter now and arrives with the rest.

A ratio rather than the two raw rates it replaced, which could not be compared by eye when hits and misses differed by an order of magnitude.
